questions.stem: In the Transport Canada abandon-ship sequence, what is done with the passengers before the abandon order is called?
options: They stay below with lifejackets in their laps until the raft inflates
They are sent into the water to swim out to the raft
They gather on deck, dressed warmly in lifejackets, and are counted
They put lifejackets on only after the abandon order is called
questions.explanation: The sequence has passengers muster on the main deck, dressed warmly with lifejackets on (not donned indoors), and has the crew confirm everyone is accounted for, while the raft, medical kit, blankets, food and EPIRB are made ready.

questions.stem: Which of these is gathered to load into the life raft in the Transport Canada sequence?
options: The anchor and the chart table
The medical kit, blankets, food and EPIRB
The galley stove, a spare gas bottle and the cooking pots
The ship's compass and the log book
questions.explanation: The sequence says to prepare the life raft and gather the medical kit, blankets, food and EPIRB to load into it. The others are not survival items.

questions.stem: The life raft is thrown over the side. Which statement matches the template?
options: It is inflated on its painter and kept alongside while safe
The painter is cut at once so the raft cannot be dragged down
The raft is paddled clear of the vessel before anyone boards
The raft is lowered empty and people jump in from the rail
questions.explanation: The template has the raft thrown over and inflated with the painter attached, kept tied to the vessel while that is safe, and cast off only if the vessel is likely to sink or capsize or alongside is hazardous.

questions.stem: When should the raft be cast off from the vessel?
options: As soon as the raft has fully inflated
Never: the painter keeps the raft safe alongside until rescue arrives
Only after the vessel has actually sunk
If she looks likely to sink or capsize, or alongside is unsafe
questions.explanation: Keeping the raft tied alongside while safe lets people board; the template says to cast off if the vessel looks likely to sink or capsize or if staying alongside creates other hazards.

questions.stem: Which situations in the Transport Canada templates are ones where the master prepares to abandon?
options: Whenever the main engine stops
Whenever the weather forecast gets worse
When flooding threatens stability, or fire may spread or explode
Whenever a passenger asks to leave the vessel
questions.explanation: The taking-on-water template says to prepare to abandon if stability is threatened, and the fire template has the master decide whether the risk of spread or explosion requires abandoning ship.

questions.stem: A 7 m passenger-carrying vessel operates in open water 4 nautical miles from shore on a coastal voyage. Under SVR s. 411, does she need a life raft?
options: Yes, because she is more than 2 nautical miles from shore
No: a vessel of 8.5 m or less is exempt from the rule
Yes, because she carries passengers for hire
No, but only if she carries a buoyant apparatus
questions.explanation: Section 411(2) exempts a vessel of not more than 8.5 m (as well as sheltered waters voyages and vessels within two nautical miles of the shore of a river or lake). For a 7 m vessel, s. 403 may then require cold-water measures.

questions.stem: A 7 m passenger-carrying vessel carries no life raft and the water is 9 degrees Celsius. What does SVR s. 403 require?
options: Gear or procedures to protect everyone from hypothermia and cold shock
Nothing at all, because a vessel of 7 m is exempt from the life raft rule
A life raft anyway, because the water is so cold
A heater in the cabin and a thermometer on deck
questions.explanation: Section 403 applies where the water temperature is less than 15 degrees Celsius and the vessel does not carry a life raft: equipment must be carried or procedures established to protect everyone from hypothermia or cold shock.

questions.stem: A tug of 10 m has a crew of two. What does SVR s. 509 require about life rafts?
options: None, because she is under 12 m in length and carries only crew
One life raft, sized for the master only
A buoyant apparatus only, in place of a raft
Rafts for all on board, as she is over 8.5 m with two aboard
questions.explanation: Section 509(1) requires a tug of more than 8.5 m with two or more persons on board to carry life rafts for all of them. The 12 m figure is for workboats generally (s. 508).

questions.stem: According to TP 14070, which statements fit a life raft on a small vessel?
options: It is preferred only in warm water, and the release works at about 40 m
It should be lashed down so it cannot float away; the release works at 1 m
Preferred in water under 15 C; the release works at about 4 m
It need not be ready for launch at short notice on a small vessel
questions.explanation: TP 14070 says life rafts are preferred where water is below 15 degrees Celsius, that a hydrostatic release operates at about 4 m, and that crews must be ready to launch the raft on a moment's notice. Lashing it down would defeat the release.

questions.stem: A 9 m vessel on a near coastal Class 2 voyage carries a manually activated EPIRB. Where should it be?
options: Locked in the chart table drawer with the manual, so it stays dry
Worn by the person on watch, or stowed ready to take when abandoning
Fixed to the mast, where it cannot be removed
Stowed in the life raft canister at all times
questions.explanation: Section 209(4) of the Navigation Safety Regulations, 2020 says the manual EPIRB, PLB or DSC handheld must be worn by the person in charge of the navigational watch or stowed so it is readily accessible for immediate use in the event of abandonment. It must also be registered with the Canadian Beacon Registry.

questions.stem: Within what time must an owner update the Canadian Beacon Registry after a change in an EPIRB's registration details?
options: Within 30 days of the change
Within 24 hours of the change
Within 12 months of the change
Before the next voyage begins
questions.explanation: Section 228(2) of the Navigation Safety Regulations, 2020 requires the registration information to be updated within 30 days after a change.

questions.stem: A person falls into cold water. What is the first threat, and roughly how long does it last?
options: Hypothermia, lasting about 10 minutes
Swim failure, lasting about an hour
Cold shock, lasting about 10 minutes
Cold shock, lasting about 1 minute
questions.explanation: The 1-10-1 principle gives about 1 minute of cold shock (control breathing and keep the airway clear), about 10 minutes of cold incapacitation and swim failure, and about 1 hour before hypothermia leads to unconsciousness.

questions.stem: A 9 m passenger-carrying vessel (15 GT or less, 12 passengers or fewer) is asked about the Fire and Boat Drills Regulations s. 26 requirement that crew be able to don immersion suits. What is the answer?
options: Section 26 applies to every Canadian vessel
Section 26 applies only to vessels with a life raft
Those Regulations exclude her; SVR s. 420 drills apply
Section 26 applies only to fishing vessels under 150 GT
questions.explanation: Section 2(2) of the Fire and Boat Drills Regulations excludes vessels of 15 GT or less that carry 12 or fewer passengers, along with fishing vessels of 150 GT or less and cable ferries. Such a vessel's emergency procedures are covered by SVR s. 420.
